notes: Conditional review relative to the stated E001, without re-auditing its source. The equation conversion, flow construction, smoothness and L2 comparison are justified, but S001 strengthens dependence on an exact initial homogeneous norm to a bound uniform over a norm ball. This unsupported quantifier change blocks N001's uniform A and hence its uniform M claim.

applicability.notes: A001 has valid substitutions and source hypotheses, but its claimed uniform-on-balls conclusion exceeds E001(i). A002 and A003 are valid as detailed below.

argument.notes: Reflection and twisting give the stated signs; the L2 product and Fourier integral reasoning, higher-order uniqueness and stability/approximation steps are valid. However the proposed common A(T,gamma,R) is not established: finiteness of a norm-dependent bound at each exact norm does not establish its boundedness for all norms in [0,R]. The finite-Fourier-sum limit in S003 can preserve an already uniform bound, but cannot create one.

dependency_closure.notes: All original direct hypotheses are used, L1 is introduced and discharged correctly, and the source-solution witness is available. The common-bound witness A in /inference/locals/4 is unsupported by the exact E001 statement; F001 and F002 consequently export an unproved uniform clause. No other producer body or new assumption is available to supply it.

packet_replay.notes: Within the conditional packet boundary, the nonuniform source bound cannot justify the required uniformly quantified A(T,gamma,R). Replay therefore stops at that mathematical gap; the packet's permission fields add no theorem. This is a sufficiency judgment, not an execution-identity claim.

statement_closure.notes: The direct input and exported statement specify the time horizon, orders, real mean-zero domains, Fourier/measure normalization, solution convention, norm topologies and constants' intended dependencies. The two-flow assertion is conditional on the displayed L2 sum bound; smooth approximation has its usual meaning of approximating the datum. The failure is proof of the uniform assertion, not a missing statement or object identification.

H002 gives gamma>0. L1 and D003 give finite homogeneous gamma norm bounded by R.

A smooth periodic datum has finite Fourier Sobolev norm at every order, with sigma>gamma>0.

conclusion_review.notes: The source supplies C([0,T];H^sigma) flows for every higher sigma. Their embeddings into H^gamma and uniqueness at gamma identify a single flow with all these regularities. Fourier Sobolev regularity and the evolution equation then yield spatial and temporal smoothness; no uniform high-order bound over all smooth q is asserted.

findings.notes: This equivalence does not follow from the actual E001(i). A_sigma is allowed to depend on the exact initial homogeneous norm. Even a finite function of that norm can be unbounded on [0,R]. No monotonicity, local boundedness, or estimate uniform for ||q||dotHgamma<=R is stated or proved. Thus the common witness A(T,gamma,R), and the associated uniform conclusion for M, remain unsupported. Repair requires a legitimate bound with the needed uniform quantifiers or an actual derivation from the allowed inputs; simply asserting equivalence cannot discharge it.

background_notes.fact: On the normalized torus the map Jf(x)=-f(-x) is an involutive isometry on every Fourier H^s and mean-zero dot H^s; S_t is an isometry on these spaces, preserves reality and mean zero, and is strongly continuous in t.

grounds.reason: Fourier coefficients and real/mean-zero conditions are defined.
The norms are weighted square sums with even weights.
S_t has multiplier exp(i t k^3).

background_notes.justification: The coefficient of Jf is -hat f(-k); reindexing k to -k preserves the even weighted square sums. The S multiplier has modulus one and its values at opposite k are conjugate. For fixed f, each coefficient varies continuously in t, and the squared weighted differences are bounded by four times the summable norm series, giving strong continuity by a finite-tail argument.

background_notes.fact: For C([0,T];L2) periodic paths, products are C([0,T];L1), each product Fourier coefficient is continuous and bounded by the product of L2 norms, and coefficientwise integral evolution implies the corresponding space-time distributional evolution. J converts U_t=U U_x+U_xxx into u_t+u_xxx=partial_x(u^2)/2; the supplied twist gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2 as a distributional identity.

grounds.reason: The positive-order source flow is continuous and satisfies the coefficientwise integral equation.
gamma>0 and the source flow exist for each admitted datum, independently of uniformity.
B is the conjugated derivative of the product.

background_notes.justification: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the L1 product by ||f||2||g||2; apply it also to product differences. Fourier product coefficients have the same bound. Testing the integral coefficient equations against smooth periodic test functions is justified by their rapidly decaying Fourier coefficients and the polynomial factors from derivatives. Reflection and distributional differentiation give u_t=-U_t(t,-x), u_x=U_x(t,-x), u_xxx=U_xxx(t,-x); substituting gives the claimed equation. The scalar Fourier product rule with exp(-itk^3) cancels the linear term. Thus the same product formula defines B distributionally for these L2 inputs without assuming an unproved positive-norm product estimate.

background_notes.fact: Fourier truncations P_m q of a real mean-zero H^gamma datum are real mean-zero smooth functions, satisfy ||P_m q||Hgamma<=||q||Hgamma and converge in H^gamma. If paths converge uniformly in L2 and each has the same H^gamma bound K at every time, their limit has that bound at every time.

grounds.reason: Reality and zero mean are Fourier conditions.
H^gamma is defined by its convergent nonnegative Fourier norm series.
The argument uses Fourier truncations, uniform L2 convergence and finite nonnegative norm sums.

background_notes.justification: Truncation deletes nonnegative summands, and its norm error is the tail of a convergent series. Symmetric truncation preserves conjugate symmetry and the zero coefficient. Uniform L2 convergence implies coefficient convergence, so each fixed finite weighted norm sum of the limit is at most K^2; taking the supremum over the finite frequency intervals gives the claimed inequality. This conditional preservation fact does not establish the missing common K in the packet.

background_notes.fact: A smooth periodic function belongs to every Fourier H^s. A solution continuous into H^s for every finite s, satisfying the displayed polynomial differential evolution, is spatially and temporally smooth.

grounds.reason: The smooth-data branch applies E001 at every higher order and uses uniqueness to identify the flows.
E001 supplies the higher-order continuous flows and their integral evolution.
The Fourier Sobolev scale is fixed.

background_notes.justification: Repeated periodic integration by parts gives arbitrarily fast coefficient decay for a smooth datum. Conversely Cauchy-Schwarz shows that H^s embeds into C^j whenever s>j+1/2, by absolute uniform convergence of the differentiated Fourier series. These estimates also transfer time continuity. The equation then expresses the time derivative as a spatially smooth polynomial in spatial derivatives, continuously in time. Iterating differentiation of this polynomial equation yields all mixed time and spatial derivatives. This is conditional on the higher-order flows actually supplied by E001, not a new regularity theorem for rough flows.
